title: Smart City Travel
summary: A city transit authority is deciding how to modernize fare payment without disrupting service, excluding riders, or overcommitting to a fragile direct migration path.

sections.title: Situation
sections.narrative: The current bus network relies on cash and plastic transit cards. The modernization aim is to introduce app-based and bank-card contactless payment while preserving reliable, accessible public service.

entries.text: full open-loop contactless payment with bank cards and phones
legal approval for account-based fare processing
buses must continue operating without downtime
elderly and unbanked riders must not be excluded
public transit authority and private bus operators
transit system and the banking/payment system
policy questions of inclusion and privacy
advance to full account-based open-loop payment
direct shift to open-loop bank-card payment

candidate_paths.title: Path A: staged modernization route
candidate_paths.narrative: This path upgrades the existing system in stages, preserving continuity and inclusion while creating a later route into full open-loop payment.
highlights: legacy fare system to improved closed-loop card system
hybrid card plus compatibility tools before full open-loop payment
reduce boarding time and fare evasion without breaking service

candidate_paths.title: Path B: direct open-loop route
candidate_paths.narrative: This path promises faster payoff, but it carries greater dependency and disruption risk because external readiness and public inclusion obligations are tighter.
highlights: move directly to bank-card and phone payment
depends on banking, hardware, legal approval, and adoption
